metric.name: cross_request_same_bank_preissue_wait_cycles
count_condition: the external request is resident in a controller request buffer
its current prerequisite command has no failed timing constraint above the Bank level
the current prerequisite command is blocked by a timing constraint at the decoded physical Bank
the command that most recently established that blocking Bank constraint belongs to a different nonnegative inference_request_id
metric.aggregation: sum one cycle per waiting request per controller tick satisfying every count condition

excluded: request service after its command is granted
WCK synchronization and refresh unless a distinct cross-request Bank-level constraint is the active blocker
scheduler delay when another request uses a different Bank
NoC, DMA, compute, dependency, paging, and generic controller queue delay
required_source_changes: store the source_id that last establishes each command-ready constraint at every DRAM hierarchy node
extend timing checks to return the first failing hierarchy level, decoded Bank, ready cycle, and blocker source_id
scan waiting external requests once per controller tick after prerequisite resolution and before command issue
emit per-request accumulated strict wait plus optional interval records
retain existing first_issue/final_issue/row_status fields as separate diagnostics
known_limitations: A single command-ready timestamp may be the maximum of constraints established by multiple commands; blocker ownership must follow the constraint that wins the maximum, including deterministic tie handling.
This direct metric is an attribution of observed pre-issue waiting, not by itself an end-to-end causal slowdown. A paired Bank-conflict-removal intervention remains required for the bottleneck claim.
Critical-path exposed conflict time must be computed separately; summing all request wait cycles is not a conserved wall-clock decomposition.
claim_gates: per-request strict wait is conserved against emitted interval records
normal and Bank-conflict-removal paired runs keep DAG, routing, placement, bytes, compute, NoC, paging, and random seeds identical
stacked-bar components sum to end-to-end runtime without summing overlapping request waits
Bank intervention produces a stable end-to-end reduction with paired uncertainty
